Department: Flight Operations Reports to: Manager Operations Control Direct Reports: None

1. Job purpose

The Flight Dispatcher manages the day-to-day functions of the operations control center. The Dispatcher is responsible for daily liaison with all flight crew and ensures that all flights are dispatched safely, on time and in compliance with company procedures. The Flight Dispatcher reports to the Manager Operations Control.

2. Key accountabilities

(a) Flight dispatch and release

  • Ensure smooth, efficient and timely dispatch of flights.
  • Prepare the flight release envelope and ensure all its contents are available as indicated and duly signed by the Pilot in Command (PIC) and the Flight Operations Officer (FOO).
  • Conduct pre-flight crew briefings.

(b) Flight planning and crew support

  • Assist the PIC in flight preparation by providing the relevant information required (e.g. meteorology, NOTAMs, air traffic, slots).
  • Assist the PIC in preparing the Operational Flight Plan (OFP) and manage the Air Traffic Control (ATC) flight plan.
  • Generate a manual OFP when the automated OFP is not available, taking into account prevailing weather conditions and statistical winds.
  • Supply the PIC in flight with all needed technical information via radio.
  • Support wet-leased operators with operational information.

(c) Operational monitoring and emergency response

  • Monitor and identify any operational or technical event that could disrupt the regularity of flights and take mitigating action in line with approved company procedures.
  • In the event of an emergency, initiate the applicable procedure.
  • Arrange safe and reliable transport for crew on duty to and from work during duty time.

(d) Scheduling, reporting and coordination

  • Maintain the daily flight schedules in conjunction with other departments, especially Maintenance.
  • Prepare the daily on-time performance report for onward transmission to the Manager Operations Control.
  • Prepare the monthly on-time performance report.
  • Take charge of day-to-day liaison with other company operational departments.

3. Minimum qualifications and experience

  • Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Aviation Management, Flight Operations, Aeronautical Science, Meteorology or another relevant discipline from a recognized institution.
  • Flight Operations Officer License or Airline Transport Pilot License.
  • Adequate knowledge of the Uganda Civil Aviation Regulations.
  • Excellent communication skills.
  • Thorough knowledge and understanding of flight scheduling and fleet operations.
  • Computer literate.
  • High level of proficiency in English.

4. Knowledge, skills and competencies

  • Flight scheduling and fleet operations
  • Flight planning, OFP and ATC flight plan management
  • Uganda Civil Aviation Regulations
  • Operational monitoring and disruption management
  • Emergency response
  • Clear communication with flight crew and operational departments
  • Proficiency in English
  • Computer literacy
